H1 (a): pre-fix body confirmed via `git show origin/main:src/lib/medication-badges.ts` (`cleaned.match(/(\d+)\s*mg/i)`). Against it, "Tablets (0.5 mg, 1 mg). Take strictly after food." yields "5 mg tablet", "Ampoules (80 mg/2 mL)…" yields "80 mg", and "films (2/0.5 mg and 8/2 mg …)" yields "5 mg", so the new cases (expecting "0.5 mg tablet", null, null) fail without the fix, and the committed-record case pins the finding's exact triggers (varenicline, meloxicam, methadone, nicotine-lozenge). The corpus-wide invariant asserts the real failure class (badged number must be a whole token, not a decimal tail, not a concentration, not half a combination).

H1 (b): behaviour beyond the finding, all conservative: `\bmg\b` word boundary; dose-style tokens such as "mg/day"/"mg/kg" are now skipped as non-strengths; a concentration-only or combination-only text now yields no badge instead of the descriptive first-sentence fallback (implementer disclosed this). Independent corpus comparison (old vs new function over both quick and Oral-routes sources): 80 labels change, 50 to a numeric strength and 30 to no badge (implementer said 46/34 — a counting difference, not a behavioural one). Unit stays mg-only rather than widening to mcg/g, which is narrower than the fix-sketch option and safe. No first-number fallback was added (package note honoured).

H1 residual, pre-existing and outside the finding: list-tail shapes still badge the last number rather than the first, e.g. morphine "Tablets IR (10, 20 mg)" → "20 mg tablet", levetiracetam "Tablets (250, 500, 1000 mg)" → "1000 mg tablet", risperidone "Tablets (0.5 to 4 mg)" → "4 mg tablet" (was "5 mg tablet", so strictly better). These are real strengths that exist, pass the new invariant, and were the same before this branch; worth a follow-up finding, not a blocker here.

H2 (a): pre-fix SEVERITY_TONE.low/none/safe/beneficial were "success" (visible in the diff), so the new tone assertions, the mesalazine+digoxin composed-verdict assertion (`verdict.tone` not success with `incomplete` false) and the DOM assertions (data-tone not success, band text and aria-label not matching /no alert found/i, "1 interaction" still present) all fail without the fix and assert the exact failure the finding describes. The narrowing guard (sertraline+paracetamol still renders "No alert found"/"No interaction found") is present.

H2 (b): `info` sits at priority 1 in SEMANTIC_TONE_PRIORITY, below neutral (2) and success (3), not between caution and success as the package note asked; the implementer could not change src/lib/semantic-tone.ts (not owned) and flagged it. I checked whether this ranking gap can bite today: composeMedicationVerdict's candidates are `considerationTone` (medication-patient-alerts.ts `considerationTone()` returns only danger/clinical/warning/info) and `interactionTone` (no severity maps to success any more), so `success` can only arise from the empty-candidate default, and `info` can never be outranked by a green candidate on any current path. It is a latent risk only: if a future engine ever emitted a `success` candidate alongside a documented interaction, the all-clear headline would return. Recommend the owner-decision item (a dedicated tone ranked above success) be scheduled rather than left open-ended.

H2 (b) other effects verified: interaction rows tagged low/none/safe/beneficial now sort below a hypothetical `unknown` (neutral) row — the index has 0 unknown rows today (counts: high 226, critical 225, low 34, moderate 17, caution 12, none 9, safe 5, beneficial 3), and where one existed the composed headline would be "Manual review", which is the conservative direction. The detail-panel InlineNotice for such a row now renders info-toned with the Info icon instead of the success ShieldCheck (the finding's secondary complaint). `medicationVerdictRingClass` and `clinicalBadgeToneClass` both already handle `info`. The one pre-existing case that changes (info consideration + incomplete analysis → "Manual review") is disclosed and conservative. The #2538 guard line (`incomplete && success → neutral`) was kept and extended, so the Stage-5 package note was honoured.
